title: Differential compatibility of the constructed ordinary evaluation
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U$ an open, and $P,F$ arbitrary cochain complexes of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. Put $D_P=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,\mathcal O_U[0])$ [def-pur-hom-complex] and $T=\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D_P)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Define $E^n:T^n\to\mathcal Hom^n(P,F)$ by the coproduct and product universal properties: its $(p,q)$ tensor summand followed by the Hom projection indexed by $r$ is the ordinary evaluation component of [lem-pc-strictly-perfect-ordinary-evaluation], zero unless $r+q=0$, and otherwise the currying of evaluation on $P^r$ followed by the unit action on $F^p$. Then for every $m=n+1$, $E^n d_{\mathcal Hom}^{n,m}=d_T^{n,m}E^m$. No strict perfectness or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08DQ, proof of lemma-dual-perfect-complex, ordinary complex evaluation; section-hom-complexes, differential formula

proof.text: Use the specified product-limit projections of the Hom complex to lift the maps to every internal-Hom factor. Descend the resulting maps out of the total-tensor coproduct. These are real graded maps E^n; the two universal properties prove their prescribed summand/projection formula.

Check E^n;d_H=d_T;E^(n+1) after precomposition with each summand F^p tensor Hom(P,O[0])^q and projection to the factor indexed by r. Use the product and coproduct hom-ext principles. Expand d_T=d_F tensor 1+(-1)^p 1 tensor d_dual and d_H=d_F composed with the map minus (-1)^(p+q) precomposition with d_P.

Naturality of the sheaf tensor-Hom bijection and of the unit action identifies the d_F contributions. Since O[0] has zero differential, d_dual(phi)=-(-1)^q phi composed with d_P. The tensor sign multiplies this by (-1)^p, giving the required -(-1)^(p+q). For r+q=0 only the d_F contributions remain; for r+q=-1 only the d_P contributions remain; all other projected contributions are zero. Proof irrelevance identifies the degree transports. Thus every projected summand agrees. Empty opens and zero complexes give zero maps by the same formulas.
